key_insight: CA-WCP adds class-aware, asymmetric conformal uncertainty to 3D segmentation so volume bounds stay calibrated even under distribution shift.
clinical_relevance: It can make volumetric tumor or organ segmentation more trustworthy and easier to communicate in uncertainty-aware radiology workflows.
method: Uses latent-space density-ratio weighting to handle covariate shift.
Builds separate lower and upper volume bounds with directional quantiles.
Adjusts each class with an asymmetry factor from validation false-positive and false-negative rates.
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2020 and a synthetic multi-organ CT benchmark, the observed 90% coverage intervals contained the nominal level for every class, with 8–14% narrower intervals than symmetric weighted conformal prediction.
watch_item: Performance depends on representative validation data for class asymmetry and shift estimation, so calibration may weaken if those assumptions do not hold.
paper_title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
